Automotive Confidentiality Notice: Proprietary OEM client vehicle CAD assets and confidential specs are generalized for public portfolio presentation. The user research, 3D interaction model, and frontend WebGL implementation documented here reflect my actual hands-on work.

3D Vehicle Configurator & Real-Time X-Ray Diagnostics

Designing and coding an in-browser 3D automotive experience that eliminates WebGL performance lag and lets users inspect internal mechanical subsystems with instant X-ray shaders.

FIG 1.0 · ACTUAL PRODUCTION INTERFACE DESIGNED AND CODED Featuring dual Assembled / X-Ray mode, 3D hotspots, and subsystem spec drawer
{/* ===================================================== 01. THE PROBLEM: UNDERSTANDING WITH THE PM ====================================================== */}
{getSectionTag("01 · THE PROBLEM: WHY & HOW")}

Sitting with the PM to understand the real problem

Before writing a single line of code or designing mockups, I sat down with the Product Manager to dissect why existing 3D automotive tools were failing users and how we could deliver real value:

1. The User Need

Automotive clients, technical buyers, and mechanics didn't just want to rotate a shiny car exterior. They needed to explore the engineering inside: cooling loops, radiators, direct injection, and turbo air intake.

2. The Constraint

They didn't want users downloading bulky 10GB CAD software or desktop executables. The entire experience had to run smoothly in standard web browsers on everyday laptops.

3. The Bottleneck

Raw CAD models have millions of polygons. Loading them in WebGL caused 5-second browser freezes, memory crashes, and 15fps stutter during camera rotations.

{/* ===================================================== 02. THE SOLUTION: DESIGN & INTERACTION ====================================================== */}
{getSectionTag("02 · DESIGN & INTERACTION ARCHITECTURE")}

Designing an intuitive dual-mode spatial UI

I designed the interface around spatial clarity so non-technical users and engineers alike could explore systems effortlessly:

Instant Dual-Mode Toggle

A clean toggle at the top switches between Assembled Mode (full exterior gloss styling) and X-Ray Mode (ghosted semi-transparent car body highlighting mechanical subsystems).

3D Coordinate-Anchored Hotspots

Hotspot callout lines project directly from 3D world coordinates (e.g. front radiator tank) and track smoothly with the user's camera orbit, clicking directly into component details.

Technical Specification Drawer

A dedicated slide-in panel reveals component location, operating media (water / ethylene glycol), ID dimensions (25–51 mm), temperature ratings, and isolated 3D component renders.

Bottom Subsystem Carousel

Organized horizontal cards let users jump directly between Cooling & Thermal, Air Intake & Charge Air, and Fuel & Gas Delivery without hunting across the vehicle.

{/* ===================================================== 04. FRONTEND ENGINEERING & 3D OPTIMIZATION ====================================================== */}
{getSectionTag("04 · FRONTEND DEVELOPMENT & WEBGL")}

How I solved real-time 3D performance in code

Designing a 3D interface is useless if the browser stutters at 15fps. Because I handled the frontend development, I took direct responsibility for 3D asset optimization and WebGL rendering:

1. Retopology & Normal Baking

Raw CAD models were retopologized into clean low-poly meshes. I baked high-poly geometric bevels into normal maps, cutting memory overhead by 65% while keeping realistic lighting.

2. Custom Dual-Mode Shaders

Wrote custom shaders that toggle seamlessly between a high-gloss clearcoat car paint and a ghosted semi-transparent Fresnel X-ray shader without reloading the 3D scene.

3. Smooth Camera Rig with Inertia

Engineered camera orbital controls (3D, Front, Side, Rear) with inertial damping, ensuring smooth inspection without sudden camera snapping.

4. Silky 60fps WebGL Execution

Tested across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox to ensure stable 60fps frame rates on standard laptops without draining battery or crashing GPU threads.

{/* ===================================================== 05. REFLECTIONS ====================================================== */}
{getSectionTag("05 · REFLECTION")}

What this project taught me

Being able to both design the UI in Figma and code the frontend in WebGL/React changes how you solve problems:

  • Understanding Technical Limits Breeds Better UI: Instead of designing impossible 3D animations that freeze the browser, I designed around shader capabilities from day one.
  • PM Collaboration Solves the Right Problem: Asking why upfront saved weeks of work. We didn't need another generic car customizer—we needed an internal mechanical inspection tool.
